title: Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching of DAGLα in Mouse Neurons
author: Yoon, Penzes

steps.title: Coat coverslips with poly‑D‑lysine
steps.instruction: Sterilize 12 mm No. 1.5 coverslips in 100 % ethanol for 10 min, UV‑irradiate overnight, then apply 1 mL of 0.2 mg/mL PDL solution per well in a 12‑well dish; incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Next day collect PDL, store at –20 °C (reuse up to 5 times within 3 months). Wash coverslips 3 × with 1 mL autoclaved milli‑Q water, aspirate, air‑dry, seal with parafilm and store at –20 °C (use within a week).

substeps.instruction: a. Place coverslips in 100 mm petri dish, add ethanol, agitate 10 min, UV overnight.
b. Transfer coverslips to a 12‑well dish, add 1 mL 0.2 mg/mL PDL per well, incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
c. Collect remaining PDL, store at –20 °C; wash coverslips 3 × with 1 mL water, aspirate, dry, seal with parafilm.

steps.title: Seed HEK293T cells on coated coverslips
steps.instruction: Maintain HEK293T cells in 100 mm dishes; when cultures reach 80–90 % confluence, detach cells and seed 2 % of the total cell number onto each PDL‑coated coverslip.

steps.title: Transfect HEK293T cells with SEP‑DAGLα
steps.instruction: One day after seeding, prepare PEI transfection: mix 50 µL 2× PEI (2 µg/µL, total 100 µg) with DMEM in a 1.5 mL tube; in another tube mix 1 µg p3XFlag‑SEP‑DAGLα plasmid with 50 µL DMEM. Combine, vortex, incubate 37 °C ≥20 min. Adjust each well to 400 µL (preferably by reducing existing media), add the mixture dropwise onto each coverslip, and after ≥4 h replace with 1 mL DMEM containing 5 % FBS and penicillin/streptomycin. Incubate 36–48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: a. Prepare 50 µL 2× PEI (2 µg/µL) in DMEM (total 100 µg).
b. Prepare 1 µg plasmid in 50 µL DMEM.
c. Combine solutions, vortex, incubate 37 °C ≥20 min.
d. Adjust well volume to 400 µL, add transfection mix dropwise, replace media after ≥4 h with 1 mL DMEM (5 % FBS + P/S).

steps.title: Prepare transfection reagents for neurons
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions: (a) transfection neurobasal medium (Neurobasal + 1× B27 + 1× GlutaMAX); (b) H‑DMEM (DMEM + 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.2–7.6); (c) Lipofectamine 2000; (d) plasmids pEZ‑3xFlag‑SEP‑DAGLα and pmCherry‑C1. Dispense 400 µL transfection neurobasal medium into each well of a 12‑well plate and pre‑warm at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Ensure the transfection media contain no antibiotics.

steps.title: Mix DNA and Lipofectamine for neurons
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, prepare two 50 µL tubes per sample: one with 50 µL H‑DMEM, the other with 50 µL transfection neurobasal medium. Add a total of 2 µg plasmid DNA (e.g., 1 µg SEP‑DAGLα + 1 µg mCherry) to the neurobasal tube; add 2 µL Lipofectamine 2000 to the H‑DMEM tube. Pipette each tube to mix, then combine the two tubes, vortex/pipette, and incubate 20–30 min at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: a. Tube 1: 50 µL H‑DMEM + 2 µL Lipofectamine 2000.
b. Tube 2: 50 µL transfection neurobasal medium + 2 µg plasmid DNA.
c. Mix tubes, vortex, incubate 20–30 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Add transfection mix to neuronal coverslips
steps.instruction: While the DNA‑Lipofectamine complex incubates, transfer neuronal coverslips to a fresh 12‑well plate containing 400 µL pre‑warmed transfection neurobasal medium using autoclaved fine forceps. After the 20–30 min incubation, dispense 100 µL of the transfection solution onto each coverslip dropwise with a 200 µL pipette tip; return plates to the incubator for 4 h.

steps.title: Post‑transfection neuronal culture
steps.instruction: After 4 h, move each coverslip back to its original 12‑well plate (containing maintenance medium) with autoclaved forceps; incubate in a humidified 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for ~48 h to allow fluorescent protein expression.

steps.title: Acquire FRAP images
steps.instruction: Perform fluorescence recovery after photobleaching on transfected HEK293T cells or primary cortical neurons as illustrated in Figure 1; after imaging, fix samples with 4 % paraformaldehyde and confirm surface SEP expression by immunocytochemistry (Figure 5).

steps.title: Open FRAP images in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Launch ImageJ and open the FRAP image stack files.

steps.title: Define ROI for bleached area
steps.instruction: Use the ROI Manager (Analyze → Tools → ROI Manager) to draw a region of interest over the bleached area; press Ctrl + t or click the Add [t] button to record the ROI.

steps.title: Copy ROI to background region
steps.instruction: Duplicate the ROI and place it over a non‑fluorescent background area to obtain background intensity values.

steps.title: Set measurement parameters
steps.instruction: Select Analyze → Set Measurements and check ‘Mean intensity’ (no other options needed).

steps.title: Measure fluorescence over time
steps.instruction: Choose Multi‑Measure; for each time point select the plane with the strongest intensity and record both the ROI and background measurements; repeat for all frames.

steps.title: Normalize fluorescence values
steps.instruction: Subtract the background mean from each ROI measurement, then divide by the pre‑bleached baseline mean; express the result as % of maximum intensity.

steps.title: Import data into GraphPad Prism
steps.instruction: Open GraphPad Prism, create a new grouped table, and import the time (X) and normalized fluorescence (Y) columns.

steps.title: Fit FRAP curves with one‑phase association
steps.instruction: In Prism, select Analyze → XY analyses → Nonlinear regression (curve fit) → Exponential → One‑phase association; run the fit to obtain plateau, mobile/immobile fractions, and half‑life (t½).

steps.title: Interpret curve‑fit parameters
steps.instruction: Calculate immobile vs. mobile fractions from the plateau values and read t½ as the time to reach half‑maximal fluorescence; compare these parameters across experimental conditions (e.g., drug treatment, mutations, knockdown).

description: The protocol describes the practical steps required for generating SEP–DAGLα by inserting SEP sequences into the first extracellular domain of DAGLα. To confirm the newly created SEP-DAGLα, the plasmid was transfected into HEK293T cells, and then the FRAP assay was performed (Figure 1). After the experiment, the sample was fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA), and the surface expression of SEP was confirmed through immunocytochemistry (Figure 5).Figure 1Schematic of expression and functional tests of SEP-DAGLα
